text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on August 13 in history:
**1521 - Hernando Cortes, Spanish conqueror, captured and destroyed Tenochtitlan (Mexico City) after a three month siege.
**1624 - Cardinal Richelieu was appointed Chief Minister of France by Louis XIII.
**1704 - French and Bavarian forces were routed by a combined British, German and Dutch army at Blenheim, Germany. The victors lost 6,000 soldiers compared with 21,000 French and Bavarian troops.
**1788 - Prussia joined an Anglo-Dutch alliance to form the Triple Alliance to prevent the spread of the Russo-Swedish War of 1788-90.
**1792 - Revolutionaries imprisoned the French royal family.
**1814 - The Cape of Good Hope was formally ceded to the British by the Dutch.
**1818 - Lucy Stone, American feminist, born. Founder of the American Woman's Suffrage Association.
**1820 - Sir George Grove, British musicologist, born. Editor of Dictionary of Music and Musicians, the latest revised editions of which still carry his name.
**1826 - Rene Laennec, French physician and inventor of the stethoscope, died.
**1860 - Annie Oakley born as Phoebe Anne Oakley Moses. She was a markswoman and member of Buffalo Bill Cody's "Wild West Show" which toured America. Heroine of the musical "Annie Get Your Gun".
**1868 - Beginning of a series of earthquakes in Peru and Ecuador which killed about 25,000.
**1871 - German politician Karl Liebknecht born. An opponent of Germany's involvement in World War One, he and Rosa Luxemburg were founders of the Spartacus Union. Both were murdered in 1919.
**1888 - John Logie Baird, Scottish engineer and pioneer of television, born.
**1898 - U.S. forces under George Dewey captured Manila during the Spanish-American war after a three-month blockade of Manila Bay.
**1899 - Alfred Joseph Hitchcock, Hollywood film director of such classics as "The Thirty-Nine Steps", "Psycho" and "The Birds", born in England.
**1902 - Felix Wankel, German engine designer made famous for the rotary-piston engine that bears his name, born.
**1910 - Florence Nightingale, British nurse in the Crimean War, died.
**1912 - Jules Massenet, French composer of the opera "Manon", died.
**1913 - Archbishop Makarios, first president of Cyprus, born. Along with George Grivas, he was a leader of the guerrilla campaign against the island's British colonial rulers.
**1914 - France declared war on Austria-Hungary, leading to World War One.
**1923 - Mustafa Kemal Ataturk was elected President of Turkey.
**1927 - Fidel Castro, Cuban revolutionary who fought and eventually overthrew the regime of President Batista, born.
**1946 - H.G. Wells, British writer and author of works including "The War of the Worlds" and "The Shape of Things to Come", died.
**1961 - The border between East and West Berlin was closed at the Brandenburg Gate, heralding the construction of the Berlin Wall.
**1964 - The last hangings in Britain took place when two men were executed for murder at Liverpool and Manchester.
**1993 - Over 120 people died in a hotel collapse in Thailand.
**1994 - NATO Secretary-General Manfred Woerner, who led the 16-nation Western alliance through the end of the Cold War, died of cancer.
**1996 - Data sent back by the Galileo space probe indicated there may be water on one of Jupiter's moons, heightening the possibility it could support a primitive life form.
